::: {#xp-guide-library-databases}
:::

::: {.contribution authors="editorial"}

Resource source: Literature databases and access links provided by the XJTLU Library.

:::

::: {.contribution authors="unknown" status="unverified"}

When you are on the campus network, most papers in journals subscribed to by the university can be downloaded directly from the journal's website. However, (1) some publishers' websites do not recognize your IP address, even well-known titles such as the Annual Review series; and (2) you may want to download papers while off campus. That is when the library's literature databases come in useful.

![Library e-journals](../../../assets/imported/Kai.Wu/library-ejournal.jpg)

The option I use most is e-journal on the home page at <https://lib.xjtlu.edu.cn>. Search for a journal by name and follow the dedicated access link. The library also provides many full-text databases, including Chinese journal databases such as CNKI. For detailed instructions, see previous library training at <https://core.xjtlu.edu.cn/course/view.php?id=905>, or find the slides directly in this project's GitHub repository ([link](https://github.com/kaiwu-astro/xp_pgrs_unofficial_guide/tree/main/fileshare)).

:::
